<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - Sonic is a research‐grade inference pipeline for audio-driven portrait animation (CVPR 2025).  
   - It is not a multi-service web app but a modular ML inference system with both CLI and Gradio-based frontends, a preprocessing step, a core diffusion-based animation pipeline, and post-processing components.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top‐level scripts:  
     • demo.py / demo.sh – command-line entry point  
     • gradio_app.py – interactive web UI via Gradio  
   - config/inference – YAML configs for models and hyperparameters  
   - src/:  
     • dataset/face_align – face detection & alignment (yoloface, align.py)  
     • models/  
       – audio_adapter (audio_proj, audio_to_bucket)  
       – base (attention processors, UNet 3D blocks, spatio-temporal conditioning)  
     • pipelines/pipeline_sonic.py – orchestrates the core diffusion pipeline  
     • utils/  
       – RIFE frame interpolation  
       – mask_processor for compositing  
       – generic utilities  
   - examples/, requirements.txt, checkpoints/ (external model storage)

3. Key insights from README  
   - Core technologies: PyTorch, Huggingface model loading, stable-video-diffusion-img2vid-xt, Whisper, RIFE, YOLOFace.  
   - Inference workflow:  
     1. Load input image + audio  
     2. Face alignment  
     3. Audio feature extraction & bucketing  
     4. Video diffusion (UNet3D) with spatio-temporal conditioning  
     5. Frame interpolation & masking  
     6. Output video  
   - Models are downloaded via Huggingface Hub into checkpoints/.

4. Main components for the diagram  
   a. Frontend layer  
      - CLI (demo.py/demo.sh)  
      - Gradio web UI (gradio_app.py)  
   b. Preprocessing  
      - Face detector & aligner (src/dataset/face_align)  
      - Audio processor (src/models/audio_adapter: audio_to_bucket, audio_proj)  
   c. Core pipeline  
      - pipeline_sonic.py orchestrator  
      - Base modules (attention_processor, UNet_3D_Blocks, spatio-temporal conditioning)  
      - Diffusion engine (stable-video-diffusion-img2vid-xt)  
   d. Post-processing  
      - Mask processor (src/utils/mask_processor.py)  
      - Frame interpolation (RIFE: utils/RIFE/*)  
   e. Model & config storage  
      - checkpoints/ (Huggingface Hub downloads)  
      - config/inference/sonic.yaml  
   f. Output writer  
      - Video encoder (e.g., ffmpeg wrapper in demo or pipeline)

5. Relationships and interactions  
   - Frontend → Preprocessing: UI passes image/audio paths to preprocessing modules.  
   - Preprocessing → Core pipeline: Aligned face image + audio features → pipeline_sonic.  
   - Core pipeline loads model weights from checkpoints (via Huggingface Hub API).  
   - Core pipeline → Post-processing: Raw diffusion frames → mask & RIFE interpolation.  
   - Post-processing → Output writer: Final video file.  
   - Config/inference → all model modules for hyperparams and paths.

6. Architectural patterns & principles  
   - Modular pipeline pattern: clear separation of stages (preprocess/core/postprocess).  
   - Dependency injection via YAML config.  
   - Pluggable adapters (audio_adapter, base UNet blocks).  
   - Reusable utilities (RIFE, mask processor) abstracted under utils/.

7. Relevant technologies & frameworks  
   - Python 3, PyTorch, CUDA  
   - Huggingface Hub CLI & API  
   - Gradio for web inference  
   - YOLOFace for detection, Whisper for audio (external models)  
   - RIFE for frame interpolation  
   - YAML for configuration

8. Tailoring the diagram for this full-stack inference pipeline  
   - Use a left-to-right flow showing data progression: Input → Preprocess → Model → Postprocess → Output.  
   - Group components by stage and annotate which folder they live in (e.g., src/dataset, src/models, src/pipelines).  
   - Highlight external dependencies (Huggingface Hub, GPU, ffmpeg).

9. Diagramming guidelines  
   - Components: draw each major module as a labeled rectangle (e.g., “Face Aligner (yoloface)”).  
   - Arrows: show directed data flow (e.g., aligned image → diffusion model).  
   - Storage: represent checkpoints/ as a cylinder or database icon.  
   - Color coding:  
     • Blue for data (images, audio, feature tensors)  
     • Green for compute modules (models, pipelines)  
     • Orange for storage/config (checkpoints, YAML)  
     • Purple for external services (Huggingface Hub, GPU)  
   - Shapes:  
     • Rectangles for processing modules  
     • Parallelograms for data stores  
     • Cylinders for model storage  
     • Cloud icons for external services

10. Emphasize detail and completeness  
    - Label every arrow with the data type (e.g., “audio embeddings”, “video frames”).  
    - List config parameters alongside modules that consume them.  
    - Show versioned model-loading callouts (e.g., “load unet.pth”).  
    - Capture both CLI and Gradio entry points feeding into the same pipeline.

By following these instructions you will produce a detailed, accurate architecture diagram that mirrors Sonic’s modular inference workflow, highlights all core and auxiliary components, and clearly documents data flow and external dependencies.
